mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.00% in a given month coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.00% in the current month
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, 20-day forward returns after such rate spikes are not statistically different from pre-rate-spike periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly UNRATE falls by more than 0.30 percentage points from the prior month, labor market slack increases, reducing investor optimism and producing a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: In regimes with high unemployment, the predicted negative returns do not materialize, or the effect size is insignificant (p > 0.10) in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly rise in HOUST (household spending index) above 100 for three months predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals sustained consumer demand growth.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return does not exceed the 95th percentile of baseline periods with similar HOUST momentum (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO (industrial production index) below 101 for two consecutive months, while GDP momentum remains flat, predicts a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as it indicates supply-side weakness.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO month-over-month < 101 for 2 consecutive months and GDP momentum flat
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is positive in >70% of such supply contractions (out-of-sample), or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 3.50% for three consecutive months in a non-recessionary regime, the persistent easing supports risk-on sentiment, producing a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: Over 24 months, the average 60-day forward return during such periods is not statistically higher than during pre-easing baselines (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in PAYEMS (employment months) above 160,000 in a month, following a downward trend in UNRATE, indicates a labor market transition that precedes a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above 160,000 and UNRATE month-over-month < previous month
failure_condition: The predicted positive return does not occur in >50% of such labor transition events (out-of-sample).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly declines in GDPC1 (real GDP chainless) of at least 2% for two months, without a corresponding drop in CPIAUCSL, signal deflationary pressure and a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 month-over-month < -2% for 2 consecutive months and CPIAUCSL month-over-month >= -1%
failure_condition: In deflationary regimes, the negative return does not materialize, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A double-dip contraction in RSAFS (retail sales index) below 700 for two consecutive months, accompanied by a rise in CPIAUCSL above 325, predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals weak demand and inflationary pressure.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS month-over-month < 700 for 2 consecutive months and CPIAUCSL month-over-month > 325
failure_condition: The predicted negative return fails to occur in >60% of such events, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.10).
